purpose: If Gate010 shows that adaptive codebook A4 transfers to the true BitLinear activation-quantization sites, test the strongest immediate scalar-quantizer objection: whether the gain is only relative to absmax A4 and disappears against the per-token absmean INT4 rule used by BitNet v2.
entry_condition: Gate010 must pass its frozen adaptive-vs-dynamic-absmax and absolute-viability rules on both WikiText-2 and C4. Otherwise do not run Gate011.

frozen_protocol.calibration_transfer: WikiText validation only; frozen unchanged for C4
frozen_protocol.data_construction: Exactly the Gate010 token construction and first-16-sequence prefixes of the previously frozen 32-sequence tensors.

absmean_A4_definition.source_boundary: Use the BitNet v2 INT4 scalar rule at the same BitLinear activation inputs, without adding Hadamard transforms or retraining.
absmean_A4_definition.formula: For each token x: beta = mean(abs(x)); scale = sqrt(7)/(beta + eps); q = round(x*scale).clip(-8,7); return integer q and scale. The BitLinear output is dequantized by the existing post_quant_process path.
absmean_A4_definition.epsilon: Match the numerical floor convention used by the Gate010 implementation where needed for finite arithmetic.

adaptive_quantizer: Identical frozen Gate010 16-entry per-BitLinear absolute clip codebooks and per-token MSE-only codebook selection. No retraining, labels, logits, downstream loss, or evaluation-corpus tuning.

primary_rules.adaptive_beats_absmean: On each corpus, adaptive-codebook A4 mean NLL < per-token-absmean A4 mean NLL and the paired-bootstrap 95% upper CI of adaptive-minus-absmean per-sequence NLL is < 0.
primary_rules.adaptive_beats_absmax_sanity: Gate010 adaptive-vs-absmax direction reproduces on the identical slices within numerical tolerance.
primary_rules.absolute_viability: On each corpus, adaptive-codebook A4 NLL <= native A8 NLL + 0.50.
primary_rules.robust_pass: All three rules pass on both corpora.

interpretation_boundary.pass: Adaptive clip-codebook selection adds value beyond both absmax A4 and the BitNet-v2-style per-token absmean scalar rule at the native BitLinear sites. This still does not establish superiority to BitNet v2 as an architecture, because BitNet v2 uses H-BitLinear and INT4 continue-training.
interpretation_boundary.fail: Narrow or stop the adaptive-codebook method claim: if absmean matches or beats it, the surviving Gate010 effect is a baseline-selection effect rather than evidence for a distinct adaptive clipping method.
interpretation_boundary.hadamard_caveat: Do not transplant H-BitLinear into the frozen b1.58 checkpoint as a supposedly function-preserving baseline. BitNet v2 changes selected projections with an online Hadamard transform and then trains/continue-trains that architecture; direct insertion into the frozen b1.58 checkpoint would test a different, untrained function.
interpretation_boundary.shape_gain: Gate009 remains binding; do not reopen separately coded radius/shape-gain.

literature_boundary: BitNet b1.58 official packed inference is W1.58A8 with per-token absmax activation quantization.
BitNet v2 uses per-token absmax for INT8 but per-token absmean for INT4, and H-BitLinear applies an online Hadamard transform at selected projections followed by INT4 continue-training.
TWLA already demonstrates W1.58A4 PTQ using orthogonal shaping and mixed-precision allocation.
InfoQuant and related PTQ work already establish that activation-distribution shaping and quantizer-facing range design matter at A4; no broad novelty claim is permitted.
prohibitions: Do not run Gate011 if Gate010 fails.
Do not tune the absmean rule or adaptive codebooks on evaluation NLL.
Do not call Gate011 a comparison to full BitNet v2 architecture.
Do not reopen A3/A2/A1 or the shape-gain lane.
